candidates.topic: The Antikythera Mechanism — Ancient Greek Computer
candidates.teaser: A 2,000-year-old device was pulled from the sea — and it could predict the future.
candidates.video_description: In 1901, divers discovered a corroded bronze lump off the coast of Greece. Decades later, scientists realized it was a fully functioning astronomical computer — built 2,000 years before anyone thought such technology existed. Nothing like it appeared again for over 1,400 years.
candidates.script: In 1901, divers pulled a corroded bronze lump from a Roman shipwreck near Greece. Nobody knew what it was — for decades. Then X-ray scans revealed something impossible: a fully functioning astronomical computer with 37 interlocking gears, built over 2,000 years ago. It could predict solar eclipses, track planetary motion, and calculate dates decades in advance. Nothing remotely like it appeared again for 1,400 years. So who actually built it — and what else did they know?

candidates.teaser: Your body starts producing a chemical that only corpses make — and it happens while you're still alive.
candidates.video_title: Your Body Makes a Death Chemical Right Now
candidates.video_description: Cadaverine is the molecule responsible for the unmistakable smell of decomposing flesh. What most people don't know is that living human bodies produce it too — in saliva, urine, and even breath. It's one of the chemicals that makes bad breath smell the way it does.
candidates.script: Right now, your body is producing a chemical that scientists named after corpses. It's called cadaverine — the molecule responsible for the unmistakable stench of rotting flesh. But it doesn't only come from the dead. Your saliva, urine, and breath generate it continuously. It's one of the primary compounds behind bad breath. Your body has been quietly making a death molecule your entire life — and you had no idea.

candidates.topic: The Soviet Lake That Became a Nuclear Dump — Lake Karachay
candidates.teaser: There's a lake in Russia where standing on the shore for just one hour will kill you.
candidates.video_title: The Most Polluted Lake on Earth Will Kill You Fast
candidates.video_description: Lake Karachay in Russia's Ural Mountains was used as a nuclear waste dump by the Soviet Union for decades. By the 1990s, standing on its shore for just 60 minutes would expose a person to a lethal radiation dose. In 1968, a drought caused radioactive dust to spread across half a million people.
candidates.script: There is a lake in Russia where standing on the shoreline for exactly one hour delivers a lethal radiation dose. Lake Karachay was used as a Soviet nuclear waste dump for decades starting in 1951. By the 1990s, scientists measured it as the most polluted spot on Earth. In 1968, a single drought caused radioactive dust to blow across 400,000 people. The Soviets eventually filled it with concrete — because draining it was too dangerous. What else did the Cold War bury?

candidates.topic: The Teeth That Keep Growing — Continuously Erupting Teeth in Elephants
candidates.teaser: Elephants don't get cavities — but when their last tooth wears out, they quietly starve to death.
candidates.video_title: Elephants Die Because They Run Out of Teeth
candidates.video_description: Unlike humans, elephants cycle through six sets of teeth over their lifetime. Each set moves forward like a conveyor belt as the previous one wears down. When the sixth and final set is gone — usually around age 60 to 70 — the elephant can no longer chew and slowly dies of starvation.
candidates.script: Elephants don't die of old age the way you think. They die because they run out of teeth. An elephant cycles through six sets of molars in its lifetime — each one moving forward like a conveyor belt as the last wears down. Around age 65, the sixth set is gone. The elephant can no longer chew. It slowly starves. Their entire lifespan is essentially determined by a single biological countdown. Six sets. Then nothing.

candidates.topic: The Village Where Everyone Falls Asleep — Kalachi Sleeping Sickness
candidates.teaser: In a small Kazakh village, people randomly fall unconscious for days — and doctors still have no explanation.
candidates.video_title: The Village Where People Keep Falling Asleep
candidates.video_description: In Kalachi, Kazakhstan, hundreds of residents mysteriously fell asleep for days at a time between 2010 and 2015 — waking up with no memory and sometimes hallucinating. The cause stumped scientists for years. The leading theory involves a nearby abandoned uranium mine, but the full explanation remains contested.
candidates.script: Between 2010 and 2015, residents of Kalachi — a small village in Kazakhstan — randomly collapsed and slept for days. Not metaphorically. They would fall unconscious mid-sentence, mid-walk, mid-meal. They'd wake up hallucinating, with no memory of the lost days. Over 130 people were affected across 14 separate episodes. Scientists suspected a nearby Soviet uranium mine was releasing carbon monoxide and hydrocarbons underground. But Kalachi was eventually abandoned — because nobody could guarantee it would stop.
